$comment: Browser-gate selector manifest (paul-kinlan-me-1i3). The reviewed changed-path ->
browser-spec contract the architect verdict on that bead requires: every one of the
nine tests/*.browser.mjs evidence gates maps to itself and to the source surfaces it
drives; shared inputs (built-site surfaces, the lockfile pair, this runner) fan out
to every affected spec; unrelated paths are ignored EXPLICITLY, with a reason that
the selector records - never silently treated as covered; and any path that matches
neither a trigger nor an ignore rule fails the selection closed. Adding a file to a
new top-level surface therefore breaks this tier until someone classifies it, which
is the point.
Rules:
- specs.<path>.triggers: glob patterns (see select.mjs header for semantics); a
changed path matching ANY of them selects the spec. Every spec MUST list itself.
- specs.<path>.shared: names of shared trigger groups below, expanded into triggers.
- specs.<path>.siteCoupled: the spec asserts against the BUILT site (Hugo output).
The runner builds ONCE per run (npm run build) and passes SITE_DIR to every
site-coupled spec, so the three share one fresh tree - never an older public/.
- specs.<path>.timeoutSec: per-spec hard bound; the runner kills the whole process
group when it expires.
- ignore[].paths/reason: explicit out-of-scope classification. Triggers win over
ignores (a pinned content page selects its spec even though content/** is
ignored), so ignore rules may safely be broad.
- ciPaths: the exact path filter pinned into .github/workflows/browser-gate.yml.
tests/browser-gate-select.test.mjs asserts the workflow and this list agree, so
the two cannot drift; it is the deduped union of every trigger pattern.
Deliberate cost trade (recorded on the bead): ciPaths carries the BROAD 'static/**'
filter even though the spec triggers are narrower (static/images/**, static/audio/**,
the two component assets, material.css), so a NEW file anywhere under static/ still
reaches the selector and fails closed if nobody classified it. Narrowing the CI
filter to the triggers would silently skip exactly the unclassified-new-file case
the fail-closed rule exists for. content/** is NOT in ciPaths: new posts are
ignore-classified by rule, and a spec change that pins a new page arrives through
tests/*.browser.mjs, which is filtered. Chrome stays OUT of tools/fast-gate.sh
and CHECK_CMD either way.

siteBuild.$comment: Run ONCE per browser-gate run, only when a site-coupled spec is selected, against the same pinned tree; every site-coupled spec then gets SITE_DIR=<repo>/public.

ignore.reason: content: only the six pinned pages mapped as spec triggers are browser-spec inputs; every other page is exercised by the node tier (content-*.test.mjs) and the full gate's hugo build, and no spec loads it in a browser

api: the modules browser specs actually drive (mentions.js, ask-paul.ts, activitypub-html/) are spec triggers; every other endpoint is server-side, covered by the node tier, and never loaded by a browser page
lib: the modules browser specs import (ask-paul-answer.js, ask-paul-request.js, escape.js, whatwg-flora.ts) are spec triggers; the rest is server-side, covered by the node tier
edge middleware (UA quota/translation): covered by tests/middleware-ua-quota.test.mjs; no browser spec loads it
hugo new-content templates: used by `hugo new` only, never by `hugo` build output, so no spec can observe them
dev tooling and gate scripts: not loaded by the built site or any spec; the browser-gate runner itself is a trigger via the shared 'runner' group
node-tier tests, fixtures and contracts: browser specs self-trigger through their manifest keys; node tests do not change browser behaviour
CI definitions: the browser-gate workflow is a runner-surface trigger; other workflows do not touch the built site
one-off local scripts: not part of the built site and not loaded by any spec
editor/VCS/local-state files: no effect on the built site or on any spec (.nowignore affects deploy packaging only, which no spec asserts)
documentation: not loaded by the built site or any spec
